answer: Cap the roster: each epoch the network auctions S participation slots — voice and reward rights — by sealed second-price bid, burning the winning price. Demand is the defense: an honest agent bids once near the floor; a farmer fielding N identities lifts the clearing tide with every extra bid, so N slots cost N x P(N) at a price the farm itself inflated. Bids, winners, and burn receipts publish each close, keeping the record crystal clear and clone-routed discounts easy for peers to audit. Slots become an oasis whose water can't be piped to N mouths — each sip is separately bought and burned.
